description:
FILED s474b (Fable, 2026-09-07) from the USER's question "do we declare `my` variables as integers inside `use integer`?".  ANSWER: no -- and a declaration would not help.

WHAT PCL EMITS under `use integer` (Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~1624): `$s = $s * 3 + $i / 7` -> `(+ (p-int (* (p-int $s) (p-int 3))) (p-int (truncate (p-int $i) (p-int 7))))`.  Bare CL `+ - * truncate rem` (the #1175 host leaks), every operand through `p-int` = `to-number` (a typecase) + `truncate`.  No `(declare (type â¦))` anywhere; the slot is whatever the VarAnnotator verdict gave it regardless of the pragma.

MEASURED (box under load 15, both agents running -- ratios and slopes, not absolutes; scratch ui2/nu2/*b.pl; N = 3e6 and 3e7, slope = per-iteration cost):
  loop body `$s = ($s * 3 + $i / 7) % 1000003` (plain version uses int($i/7)):
    use integer   PCL 0.92 s -> 3.93 s  = 111 ns/iter     perl 0.27 -> 2.35 s = 77 ns/iter    PCL/perl 1.44x SLOWER
    plain         PCL 0.76 s -> 2.74 s  =  73 ns/iter     perl 0.40 -> 4.41 s = 149 ns/iter   PCL/perl 2.0x FASTER
    fixed cost (runpcl of a trivial program): 0.44-0.62 s
  pure SBCL (scratch intbench.lisp, speed 3 safety 1), same body, N = 3e7:
    generic INTEGER slot, untyped + * truncate mod:   0.149 s = 5 ns/iter
    (signed-byte 64) slot + sb-c::mask-signed-field:  0.147 s   (identical)
    fixnum-declared slot:                             0.218 s   (SLOWER -- the mod/the checks)
  => SBCL's untyped integer arithmetic already takes the machine path for fixnums (with the overflow check that makes bignums exact).  A type declaration buys NOTHING here, and under the ruled no-boundary model (#1513) it would be UNSAFE: a value past 2^62 is a type error at safety 1 and memory corruption at safety 0.

THE LEVER (two halves, sized separately, hand-replaced A/B first per Â§A.0):
 (a) `use integer` operands: when the operand is a LITERAL integer or a raw-numeric slot the B-regime facts already prove (docs/raw-numeric-verdict.md), emit it BARE (or `(truncate x)` when it may be a float) instead of `(p-int x)`; keep `p-int` only for an operand the facts do not cover.  Kind-A name in Pl/Passes.pm (`int-region-raw`?); PCL_OPT=none identical; guard rows incl. a NEGATIVE (a string operand under use integer still truncates: `"3abc" * 2` is 6).  Bar: the use-integer loop at least as fast as the plain one.  Hot user: lib/Math/BigInt/Calc.pm (all its digit arithmetic is under use integer) -- a bench row.
 (b) the general finding: the plain loop is 15x the SBCL floor (73 vs 5 ns/iter) with `$s` already a raw slot -- so `p-+`/`p-*`/`p-%`/`p-/`/`p-int` on a raw-numeric operand are NOT reaching a fixnum fast path inline.  Profile ONE iteration (sb-sprof on nu2b) and say where the 68 ns go; the raw-op-family switch (Passes.pm) is the place the answer lands.  Related: #1034 (user-supplied type hints, LOW PRIORITY) -- this measurement says hints on the VARIABLE are not where the time is.
NOT in scope: the 64-bit boundary itself (#1513, documented by USER ruling).


=== DONE (s473r, 2026-09-07) ===

BOTH HALVES ANSWERED.  Half (b) SHIPPED as a RUNTIME-ONLY change (commit
5125e79c, no emission change, no generation bump); half (a) is CLOSED BY
MEASUREMENT -- the emission change it proposed is not needed.

HALF (b) -- WHERE THE 68 ns GO.  The task guessed "p-+/p-*/p-%/p-/ on a raw
operand are not reaching a fixnum fast path inline".  That is WRONG for + and
*, and the hand-replacement says so directly (ab-lisp.pl, one form at a time
in the emitted .lisp, best-of-5, 3e6 iterations of
`$s = ($s * 3 + int($i / 7)) % 1000003`, base 0.153 s = 50 ns/iteration):

    p-+ / p-* -> CL + and *        +0.8 %    <- ALREADY open-coded
    p-% -> mod                     -6.7 %
    p-/ -> CL /                   -15.7 %
    p-int -> truncate             -19.6 %
    (p-int (p-/ ..)) -> truncate  -50.4 %
    all five -> machine ops       -74.9 %

The tail declaim already inlines p-+/p-* and SBCL open-codes their numberp
test, so half the iteration was int() and `/`, which no standing bench row
contained.  TWO runtime changes:

 * p-int was ONE FULL CALL with to-number`s typecase in front of the float
   test.  It is now a typecase whose two hot arms are INLINE at the call site
   (an INTEGER is its own int(); a DOUBLE-FLOAT is one nan/inf test and a
   truncate), with a box/string/single-float/ratio one call away in
   %p-int-slow.  p-int joined the tail inline declaim.
 * %p-divide-numbers built a RATIO for `(/ 8 7)` -- a gcd and a heap
   allocation -- and then coerced it, dividing again.  Inside (signed-byte 53)
   both operands are exactly representable as doubles, so one truncate (for
   perl`s exact-division answer) plus an IEEE divide gives the identical
   double, bit for bit (verified over 14 007 pairs).  Outside that range the
   old body stands, moved to %p-divide-general so each p-/ site carries only
   the inline half.

NUMBERS (bench-exec.pl BENCH_RT_B, one transpile, two cores, interleaved
best-of-5 and best-of-7; A = the lever, B = bfa11c72; box load 2-6):

    arith    0.1109 -> 0.0515 s   B/A +115.4 % (+111.7, +115.2 on re-runs)
    useint   0.1262 -> 0.0300 s   B/A +321 % (+397, +326)
    collatz  0.5305 -> 0.4005 s   B/A +32.4 % (+38.3, +38.7)
    A/perl: arith 0.28x, useint 0.26x, collatz 0.18x

HALF (a) IS CLOSED BY THAT MEASUREMENT, not by a change.  The pragma`s
pessimisation WAS p-int`s call cost, not the p-int WRAPPING: with p-int
inline, `(p-int 3)` on a literal constant-folds and `(p-int $s)` on a raw
integer slot is ~0.7 ns.  `useint` now runs at 0.0285 s against `arith`s
0.0480 -- the pragma is 1.7x FASTER than the same loop without it, where it
was 1.5x SLOWER when this task was filed, and 3.8x faster than perl.  The bar
the task set ("the use-integer loop at least as fast as the plain one") is
MET with no `int-region-raw` emission, no Kind-A name and no generation bump.
Do not build it: it would buy the residue of an already-inlined typecase and
cost the full emission boat.

THE CONTROL-ROW LESSON, worth keeping: `cfor` read -2.3 / -10.6 / -6.7 %
across three A/B runs and contains NO p-int and NO p-/ at all.  A runtime
built from bfa11c72 plus two NEVER-CALLED functions of the same size
reproduces it (cfor -3.6 %, intloop+= -5.6 %), and a byte-identical control
pair reads intloop+= -4.3 %, intloop= +5.0 %.  A few-% move on the tightest
rows is the CORE BEING RE-LAID-OUT; size-matched inert code is the cheap
discriminator, and #986 should be read with that in mind.

Bars: gate 220 files / 7644 rows (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); full sweep
--jobs 4 GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18674 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST,
drops 5 = census; ir-conform 289/0/56/0; ir-host-leak symbol set identical to
the base; ir-inventory regenerated with no tracked change; companion --jobs 1
over op/int.t op/inc.t op/numconvert.t op/for.t op/array.t op/hash.t op/sub.t
op/method.t = every file EQUAL to its baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv row, ROW
DIFF 0/0/0/0.  Guard Pl/t/perf-levers-04.t, 45 rows / 0.5 s, inverse-verified
(exactly the 3 mechanism rows fail on a bfa11c72 extraction).  New bench rows
`arith` and `useint`.  Filed #1515 (three pre-existing >2**53 divergences).
subject: PERF LEVER (measured s474b; for the next non-engine perf round): `use integer` is a PESSIMIZATION in PCL -- its loop runs 1.5x SLOWER than the same loop without the pragma (111 vs 73 ns/iteration) and 1.4x slower than perl, because every operand is wrapped in `p-int` (to-number typecase + truncate).  Use the pragma as a FACT, not a declaration: a raw-numeric operand needs no p-int; and the plain loop is 15x the pure-SBCL floor (73 vs 5 ns) -- the op dispatch, not the variable type, is the cost
